diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then the three $2 \times 2$ matrices composed of these vectors as rows have pairwise different first (and second) right-singular vectors.
By Lemma \ref{le} vector $(\pm 1, 0)^T$ can be a right-singular vector of at most one of these three submatrices.

issues.failure_explanation: In R^2 any three vectors are linearly dependent, so pairwise non-collinear squares can have collinear pairwise sums. Counterexample: v_1^2=(1,0), v_2^2=(0,1), v_3^2=(1,2) (every planar vector is a complex square, so such v_i exist); then v_1^2+v_2^2=(1,1) and v_1^2+v_3^2=(2,2) are positively collinear, so by the paper's own SVD formula the matrices with rows (v_1,v_2) and (v_1,v_3) have the same first (and same second) right-singular vector. Hence the inference is invalid and the Lemma's conclusion is false in general.

failure_location.quote: Since $v_1^2$, $v_2^2$ and $v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear, their sums $v_1^2 + v_2^2$, $v_1^2 + v_3^2$ and $v_2^2 + v_3^2$ are pairwise non-collinear too, which finalizes the proof of the lemma.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Lemma by a statement restricted to the equality configuration actually used: for squares w_1,w_2,w_3 with p w_1+q w_2+r w_3=0 (p,q,r>0) and the prescribed magnitudes, one checks that w_i+w_j and w_i+w_k are collinear only when p=q+r and then with opposite orientation, so the second right-singular vectors of the three cross-group submatrices are still pairwise distinct; also verify that these three squares are pairwise non-collinear.
issues.overall_effect: The strictness argument in Case A of the proof of Proposition pr (that (±1,0) is a σ_2-right-singular vector of at most one of the three cross-group submatrices) rests on the Lemma and is therefore unsupported; the equality characterization in Proposition pr and hence Corollary co become unproved.
issues.title: Lemma on distinct right-singular vectors is false as stated; pairwise non-collinearity of squares does not imply non-collinearity of their pairwise sums
issues.why_classification: The general Lemma must be abandoned, but a contained replacement argument specific to the equality configuration restores the Case A conclusion without changing the main result or its proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The corresponding equality is achieved if and only if the rows of the matrix are clustered into three non-empty groups
which finalizes the proof of the equality criteria.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only that equality forces the three-group configuration (necessity). It never shows that such a configuration attains equality, i.e. that every cross-group 2x2 submatrix has σ_2^2 = 1/n, yet the Proposition claims 'if and only if', and Case A explicitly uses that all three cross-group submatrices of the equality configuration for n-1 have smallest singular value exactly 1/√(n-1). This requires a verification (e.g. that |w_i|+|w_j|-|w_i+w_j| = 2/(n-1) for all cross pairs, using p w_1+q w_2+r w_3=0) which is absent.

failure_location.quote: These three rows form the three $2 \times 2$ submatrices of $\hat{C}$ with the smallest singular value equal to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n-1}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a direct computation: with |w_1|=(p+m)/(2pm) etc. and p w_1+q w_2+r w_3=0 one gets |w_1+w_2| = (m(p+q)-2pq)/(2pqm), hence σ_2^2 = (|w_i|+|w_j|-|w_i+w_j|)/2 = 1/m for every cross-group pair and 0 for same-group pairs, proving sufficiency and the claim used in Case A.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction of the equality criterion in Proposition pr and Corollary co is unsupported, and the Case A strictness argument relies on an unproved property of the configuration.
issues.title: Sufficiency direction of the equality criterion (and attainment of σ_2=1/√(n-1) by all cross-group submatrices) is asserted but never proved
issues.why_classification: A short explicit algebraic verification fills the gap; the statement, scope and method are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us select from $w_1, \ldots, w_n$ two vectors corresponding to the first block of (\ref{blck}) and denote them by $u$ and $v$.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument selects two distinct vectors from a block, which is impossible when p=1, and for p=2 the pairwise relations together with (ws) only yield |u|+|v| = 1/n+1/p and (u,v)=|u||v|, not the individual magnitudes |u|=|v|=1/(2n)+1/(2p). Thus the stated conclusion does not follow from the written argument for small blocks (e.g. n=3 has p=q=r=1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the diagonal entries of (blck): M_ii = (4/n)(|w_i| - 1/(2n)) = 2/(pn) gives |w_i| = 1/(2n)+1/(2p) for every row in a block of size p; substituting into the off-diagonal relation then gives (u,v)=|u||v| for p≥2.
issues.overall_effect: The derivation of the individual squared magnitudes in the equality criterion is incomplete for groups of size ≤2, though the conclusion itself is correct.
issues.title: Final step of the equality analysis fails for blocks of size 1 or 2
issues.why_classification: A one-line local fix using quantities already computed in the paper closes the gap with no loss of content.
